key_insight: A two-stage "synthesize-and-reground" pipeline creates faithful, scalable QA pairs from focused document segments and programmatically re-embeds them into full-document tasks, reconciling the trade-off between scale, faithfulness, and realism for scientific multimodal reasoning datasets.
problem_solved: How to build large-scale, realistic, and faithful scientific multimodal document reasoning datasets for training foundation models without sacrificing fidelity or contextual realism.
method: Claim-Centric QA Synthesis: generate faithful, isolated QA pairs and stepwise reasoning focused on specific claims or local segments.
Document-Scale Regrounding: programmatically re-embed the isolated QA pairs into full-document tasks to restore context, coherence, and document-level challenges.
End-to-end pipeline design that balances dataset scale with faithfulness and realism for multimodal scientific documents (text + figures/tables).
impact: Enables practitioners to produce large, realistic training data for multimodal foundation models that preserve factual grounding and document-level context, improving scientific document understanding and downstream reasoning performance.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline diagram (left: Claim-Centric QA Synthesis; right: Document-Scale Regrounding) with arrows showing flow from segment to full document.
Triangle trade-off chart illustrating Scale vs Faithfulness vs Realism and how the pipeline shifts the balance.
Before/After example: isolated QA pair (with snippet) vs regrounded full-document question showing added context (include small figure/table thumbnails).
Evaluation bar chart comparing baseline dataset approaches vs synthesize-and-reground on metrics like fidelity, contextual accuracy, and scale.
paper_title: SciMDR: Benchmarking and Advancing Scientific Multimodal Document Reasoning
paper_authors: Ziyu Chen, Yilun Zhao, Chengye Wang, Rilyn Han, Manasi Patwardhan
